body:
**Short answer:** if loud music would genuinely spoil your Santorini cruise, a private catamaran is the safest choice — but only after you tell the operator that you want low background music or no party-style music.

If you are comfortable with some music and simply want to avoid a floating nightclub, a small-group cruise can work well.

What I would not do is assume that words such as **luxury**, **romantic** or **sunset** automatically mean quiet.

They do not.

## The problem is not really the boat

Two almost identical catamarans can produce completely different afternoons.

One can feel like a slow lunch at sea.

The other can end with dancing, loud music and an open bar.

The difference is often not the hull.

It is the **number of people, crew style, music policy and the particular group sharing the boat that day**.

That is why choosing only by photographs is risky.

A photograph of a white catamaran beneath the caldera tells you almost nothing about how it will sound three hours later.

## What travellers actually report

Recent reviews show why this question matters.

Some travellers describe Santorini catamaran cruises as relaxed, spacious and one of the highlights of their holiday.

Others report something very different.

On one popular sunset sailing, recent guests complained about music playing loudly for much of the trip and described the atmosphere as closer to a party boat than the romantic cruise they expected.

Another traveller on the same general type of experience enjoyed the trip but specifically mentioned that the music became uncomfortably loud on the return.

Other passengers loved exactly that energy.

They danced.

They made friends.

They thought the music made the cruise more fun.

None of those people is necessarily wrong.

They simply wanted different things.

That is why a 4.9-star rating does not answer the question:

**Will this cruise feel quiet enough for me?**

## “Luxury” does not mean quiet

This is one of the easiest booking mistakes to make.

A product may be described as:

* luxury
* premium
* romantic
* sunset
* semi-private

and still include music, drinks and a fairly social atmosphere.

Those words describe the positioning of the cruise.

They do not describe the volume.

If music matters to you, look for an actual music policy or ask the operator directly.

[Santorini Sunset Luxury Sailing Catamaran Cruise with BBQ, drinks, transfer](https://www.viator.com/tours/Santorini/Santorini-Lagoon-560-Sunset-Tour-with-BBQ-and-Drinks/d959-7207P3?pid=P00320497&mcid=42383&medium=link&medium_version=selector "affiliate-button")

## “Small group” helps — but it is not a guarantee

A smaller group usually gives you more space and less crowd pressure.

That is valuable.

But twelve or twenty people can still have a lively party if the group and crew are in that mood.

One current Spiridakos premium shared catamaran limits the group to 20 passengers.

The operator says its shared cruises use music to create a pleasant background atmosphere.

That sounds much closer to what I would choose if I wanted a sociable but not deliberately party-focused trip.

Still, I would not translate **background atmosphere** into **guaranteed quiet**.

Those are not the same thing.

## If silence matters, private changes the calculation

A private cruise costs much more.

But in this particular case you are paying for something beyond privacy.

You are paying for **control**.

Spiridakos explicitly says that private-charter guests can choose the style and energy level of the music, from calm and relaxing to a party atmosphere.

That is the clearest policy I found.

For someone who dislikes loud music rather than merely preferring something quieter, that matters more than whether the boat has slightly better food or a newer deck.

A private cruise also removes another unpredictable variable:

the strangers sharing the boat with you.

It will just be your group.

## My first shared option

### Spiridakos Premium Small-Group Catamaran

This is the shared cruise I would compare first.

The current Viator listing is approximately five hours, includes pickup, food and drinks, and has a maximum of 20 travellers.

The reason I am interested in it for this particular problem is not its rating.

It is the operator's own explanation of the atmosphere.

Shared cruises have music, but the company describes it as background atmosphere rather than giving guests control over a party playlist.

That makes it suitable if your position is:

**“Some music is fine. I just don't want five hours of nightclub volume.”**

It does **not** suit someone who requires silence.

Before paying, I would still send the operator the question near the end of this article.

**Viator product code: 17549P13**

\[AFFILIATE LINK — Premium Small-Group Catamaran Cruise]

## The option I would choose if loud music is a deal breaker

### Spiridakos Private Catamaran

This changes the risk substantially because only your own group participates.

More importantly, the operator's FAQ says private charters can choose the style and energy level of the music.

That is unusually useful information.

You still need to tell them what you want.

Do not simply book “private” and assume everyone understands your definition of relaxed.

I would write something explicit:

**low background music or no music, please — not a party atmosphere.**

The current Viator private product is listed as a private activity for your group only.

**Viator product code: 17549P8**

\[AFFILIATE LINK — Private Santorini Catamaran]

## A private alternative worth comparing

There are other private Santorini cruises that may work even if they do not publish such a clear music policy.

One current private catamaran option from Sail Away is available only to your group, and a recent 2026 reviewer specifically described the experience as a relaxing day where the crew gave the guests privacy.

That is encouraging.

But it is still not a written guarantee about music.

So I would treat this as an alternative to compare, not as a confirmed quiet cruise.

**Viator product code: 63718P6**

\[AFFILIATE LINK — Private Full-Day Catamaran]

## What I would avoid if loud music really bothers you

I would be cautious with a large shared sunset cruise where the product includes music and an open-bar/social format.

That does not mean the cruise is bad.

Some of these trips have thousands of excellent reviews.

People love the crews, food, swimming and the chance to meet other travellers.

But recent reviews also show that the same atmosphere can become much louder than some passengers expected.

A good tour can still be the wrong tour for you.

That distinction matters more to me than its star rating.

[Santorini Private Catamaran Cruise with BBQ, Open Bar & Transfers](https://www.viator.com/tours/Santorini/Santorini-sailing-catamaran-and-yacht-private-cruises/d959-17549P8?pid=P00320497&mcid=42383&medium=link&medium_version=selector "affiliate-button")

## Three questions to ask before booking

If sound matters to you, I would ask these before paying.

### Is music played throughout the cruise?

Do not ask only:

**“Is this a party boat?”**

Almost nobody markets themselves that way.

Ask about the actual music.

### Can the volume be kept low?

This is much more useful.

If the answer is vague — “the atmosphere depends on the group” — you have learned something important.

### How many passengers are normally on this departure?

Maximum capacity and normal group size are not always the same.

A boat with twenty passengers feels very different from one with fifty.

## Open bar is a clue, not proof

Many excellent Santorini cruises include wine, beer or an open bar.

That alone does not make them party boats.

But if a product combines:

**large group + sunset + open bar + onboard music**

I would expect a more social atmosphere than on a small daytime sailing.

That is an inference, not a rule.

The group on your day can still be quiet.

Or very much not quiet.

## Would a morning cruise be quieter?

Possibly.

But I could not find reliable enough evidence to tell you that morning cruises are consistently quieter than sunset departures.

It sounds logical.

That is not enough.

I would choose by group size and music policy before choosing by time of day.

## Who should choose what?

### Choose a small shared catamaran if…

You do not mind background music.

You like meeting a few other travellers.

You want to keep the price far below a private charter.

You mainly want to avoid a crowded party-boat feeling.

A maximum of around 20 guests is a sensible place to start looking.

### Choose private if…

Loud music causes you real discomfort.

You are celebrating something quietly as a couple or family.

You want control over the mood.

Or you simply do not want the quality of an expensive afternoon to depend on the group that happens to book beside you.

In that situation, private is not only a luxury upgrade.

It solves the actual problem.

### Skip the boat altogether if…

Even low music, social drinking and five hours with other people already sound exhausting.

Santorini does not require a catamaran cruise to count as a successful trip.

There are many ways to enjoy the caldera.

Spend the money on a good dinner, a winery or a quieter day elsewhere on the island.

That is also a perfectly good choice.

## The message I would send before paying

Copy this:

> We are looking for a relaxed cruise and would prefer low background music rather than loud or party-style music. Is that realistic on this departure? If we book private, can we request very low music or no music at all?

I like this better than asking whether the cruise is “relaxing”.

Relaxing means different things to different people.

This question does not.

## Dan’s recommendation

I have not taken these particular cruises myself.

I checked the current product conditions, operator information and recent traveller reviews because loud music is exactly the kind of small detail that can turn an expensive experience into the wrong one.

My choice would be simple.

If I were comfortable with quiet background music, I would start with the smaller shared Spiridakos option and confirm the atmosphere before booking.

If loud music genuinely bothered me, I would stop trying to predict the personality of twenty strangers and book private.

Not because private is automatically better.

Because it gives me control over the one thing I care about.

**If quiet matters, pay for control — not for the word “luxury”.**

## Find a boat that suits you

If you would rather compare a few Santorini boat options by group size, private/shared format and what matters to you, use the [Greece by Dan boat concierge](/concierge/).

It searches a shorter list instead of sending you through hundreds of almost identical cruise listings.
